title: B2 Real-Life Mission
description: Integrate the Unit language to complete a sustained B2 mission about advanced real-life communication.

stages.title: Understand meaning and form
stages.instructions: Read the concept, pattern, examples, contrast, common issue, and recap.

blocks.text: The communicative aim of this lesson is to integrate the Unit language to complete a sustained B2 mission about advanced real-life communication. The central language focus is integrated B2 communication review. In the context of advanced real-life communication, form and meaning work together: first identify the relationship between the ideas, then choose wording that makes that relationship clear to another person. At B2, organize the message so the listener can follow the claim, support, qualification, and practical consequence. Choose collocations and discourse markers that sound natural in professional and social contexts.

blocks.english: This example illustrates viable alternative clearly.
blocks.explanation: This model establishes the main communicative move.
This model develops or qualifies the message.

blocks.text: Start with the model “This example illustrates viable alternative clearly.” It establishes a useful direction for the exchange. The second model, “We should consider trade-off carefully.” adds another layer: a reason, implication, contrast, or response. Notice how each complete chunk does a communicative job. Practice replacing one detail while preserving the original grammar, stance, and register. Then connect the revised sentence to a relevant consequence or example instead of changing topic abruptly.

A useful pattern for this lesson is: integrated B2 communication review. Use it when the situation genuinely calls for that meaning. Contrast matters: a direct factual statement presents information, while a qualified or hypothetical form changes the speaker's commitment to it. The choice should be driven by evidence, time reference, relationship, and purpose. In listening, pay attention not only to individual words but also to linkers, stress, and the speaker's degree of certainty.

blocks.title: Contrast
blocks.text: Compare a direct statement with language shaped by integrated B2 communication review; the intended meaning determines the form.

A common issue is to select an advanced-looking form without maintaining its meaning across the sentence. That can create a mismatch in time, stance, or register. Check three things: what happened or is being proposed, how certain the speaker is, and what response is expected. For b2 real-life mission, clarity comes from a coherent message rather than maximum complexity. The later stages recycle the same vocabulary and expressions so that recognition becomes controlled production and then flexible interaction. This sixth Lesson consolidates Lessons 1–5 and introduces no major new grammar. Select among the Unit patterns according to the communicative need.

blocks.title: Common issue
blocks.text: Do not add complexity that changes the time reference, degree of certainty, or relationship with the listener.

In this situation, We should consider trade-off carefully. The discussion highlighted preferred course of action.
From another perspective, The discussion highlighted preferred course of action. A clear explanation addresses contingency plan directly.
More specifically, A clear explanation addresses contingency plan directly. The speaker emphasized resolve the matter.
Even so, The speaker emphasized resolve the matter. Our response should account for complex issue.
As a result, Our response should account for complex issue. This example illustrates root cause clearly.
